On Monday, the Wuhan Municipal Bureau of Culture and Tourism announced the conclusion of its investigation into an operatic performance by comedian Guo Degang back in July, and said that it would levy hefty fines on the organizers and theatrical venue involved. The investigation purportedly stemmed from a complaint by an unknown member of the public who alleged that Guo, one of China’s most famous comedians, had “distorted and vulgarized” a revolutionary classic by slightly altering the lyrics to a song that had once appeared in the 1956 revolutionary film “Railway Guerrilla.” The case has been cited as an example of the growing chill over various forms of expression in China.
The Wuhan investigators concluded that Guo’s performance had “caused a negative social impact,” but did not fine him personally, nor did they say whether he would face performing restrictions in the future.
